questions.answer: Nē timōris servī fīāmus.

questions.prompt: These fields are becoming barren through neglect.
questions.answer: Hī agrī neglegentiā sterilēs fīunt.

questions.prompt: He asked what would become of the captured citizens.
questions.answer: Rogāvit quid dē cīvibus captīs fieret.

questions.prompt: The frightened youth suddenly became silent when the sword was drawn.
questions.answer: Iuvenis perterritus, gladiō strictō, repente tacitus factus est.

questions.prompt: It happens that the bravest men are often made captives.
questions.answer: Fit ut fortissimī virī saepe captīvī fīant.

questions.prompt: We were growing weary, since the road had been made longer by the rains.
questions.answer: Fessī fīēbāmus, quoniam via imbribus longior facta erat.

questions.prompt: May the citizens become worthy of the freedom which was won by their fathers.
questions.answer: Cīvēs dignī fīant lībertāte quae ā patribus parta est.

questions.prompt: The waters of the river, swollen by rain, became more dangerous.
questions.answer: Aquae flūminis, imbre auctae, perīculōsiōrēs factae sunt.

questions.prompt: I fear that our allies may become enemies during the war.
questions.answer: Vereor nē sociī nostrī in bellō hostēs fīant.

questions.prompt: As winter was drawing near, the mountains became white with snow.
questions.answer: Hieme appropinquante, montēs nive albī factī sunt.

questions.prompt: Let us not become idle, lest the harvest be lost.
questions.answer: Nē ignāvī fīāmus, nē messis āmittātur.

questions.prompt: The immortal gods went into the citadel while the enemy was fleeing.
questions.answer: Deī immortālēs in arcem iērunt dum hostēs fugiēbant.

questions.prompt: When the messenger returned, he went at once to the general.
questions.answer: Nūntius rediēns statim ad ducem iit.

questions.prompt: Let us go into the woods to seek the beautiful maiden.
questions.answer: In silvam eāmus ut virginem pulchram petāmus.

questions.prompt: The soldiers were going through the forest when a great cold fell upon them.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs per silvam ībant cum ingēns frīgus eōs oppressit.

questions.prompt: I would go to Rome if I had enough money.
questions.answer: Rōmam īrem sī satis pecūniae habērem.

questions.prompt: Having set out at dawn, the traveler went on foot to the town.
questions.answer: Prīmā lūce profectus, viātor pedibus ad oppidum iit.

questions.prompt: The time for going has now come.
questions.answer: Tempus eundī iam vēnit.

questions.prompt: The king, about to go into battle, encouraged his own men.
questions.answer: Rēx, in proelium itūrus, mīlitēs suōs adhortātus est.

questions.prompt: Go, and announce these things to the immortal gods!
questions.answer: Ī, et haec deīs immortālibus nūntiā!

questions.prompt: Going toward the citadel, they saw the wounded soldier.
questions.answer: Ad arcem euntēs, mīlitem vulnerātum vīdērunt.

questions.prompt: The general approached the walls that had been captured.
questions.answer: Dux mūrōs captōs adiit.

questions.prompt: The brave men crossed the river during the night.
questions.answer: Virī fortēs flūmen nocte trānsiērunt.

questions.prompt: Many perished while the city was burning.
questions.answer: Multī periērunt cum urbs ārdēret.

questions.prompt: The city was being approached by the enemy at first light.
questions.answer: Urbs ab hostibus prīmā lūce adībātur.

questions.prompt: He asked the guards where we were going by night.
questions.answer: Custōdēs rogāvit quō nocte īrēmus.

questions.prompt: If you had gone with me, you would have seen the temple.
questions.answer: Sī mēcum īssēs, templum vīdissēs.

questions.prompt: You must go to the forum tomorrow.
questions.answer: Tibi crās in forum eundum est.

questions.prompt: The old man kept going out of the house every day.
questions.answer: Senex cotīdiē ē domō exībat.

questions.prompt: Go forth, soldiers, and defend the fatherland!
questions.answer: Exīte, mīlitēs, et patriam dēfendite!

questions.prompt: We do not know whether the enemy will go away.
questions.answer: Nescīmus num hostēs abitūrī sint.

questions.prompt: The general's son will go out of the camp before dawn to scout the enemy's forces.
questions.answer: Fīlius ducis ante lūcem ē castrīs exībit ut cōpiās hostium explōret.

questions.prompt: If the envoys had gone away sooner, they would not have perished.
questions.answer: Sī lēgātī citius abiissent, nōn periissent.

questions.prompt: Let us go through the forest by a hidden route, lest the guards see us.
questions.answer: Per silvam occultō itinere eāmus, nē custōdēs nōs videant.

questions.prompt: The old king, about to go into exile, addressed the citizens with a sad voice.
questions.answer: Rēx senex, in exsilium itūrus, cīvēs trīstī vōce adlocūtus est.

questions.prompt: While the crowd was going into the temple, a serpent suddenly appeared.
questions.answer: Dum turba in templum ībat, serpēns subitō appāruit.

questions.prompt: Go, companions, and return before the sun sets!
questions.answer: Īte, comitēs, et redīte antequam sōl occidat.

questions.prompt: We asked the merchant where he was going with so many wares.
questions.answer: Mercātōrem rogāvimus quō cum tot mercibus īret.

questions.prompt: The philosopher, about to go away, gave many gifts to his disciples.
questions.answer: Philosophus, abitūrus, discipulīs suīs multa dōna dedit.
